_about: What the document model may say a document states. Each predicate is a kind of statement from the kinds below (each naming the inference families that consume it and the vocabulary term it follows), the OAM asset types its subject and object may be, and, when the statement is the same fact as an OAM relation, that relation's label and direction (forward: subject --label--> object; inverse: object --label--> subject). A test checks every OAM mapping against the OAM relationship table. detail is the extra text a predicate carries, such as the title of a role. categories are what a document may be (a File is_a statement). The model's statements are validated against this file and quote a stored passage exactly; a statement is evidence for inference, never a fact on its own. Add predicates and categories here, not in Go code.

predicates.name: subsidiary_of
predicates.description: The subject is a subsidiary company of the object.

predicates.name: unit_of
predicates.description: The subject is a division, department, campus, branch or other unit of the object.

predicates.name: owned_by
predicates.description: The subject is owned by the object.

predicates.name: operated_by
predicates.description: The subject is run or managed by the object on its behalf.

predicates.name: member_of
predicates.description: The subject is a member of the object (a person on its staff or board, an organization in a consortium).

predicates.name: holds_role
predicates.detail: the title of the role, as written
predicates.description: The subject holds a named role (title) at the object.

predicates.name: funded_by
predicates.description: The subject receives funding, a grant or sponsorship from the object.

predicates.name: partner_of
predicates.description: The subject works in partnership or collaboration with the object.

predicates.name: supplied_by
predicates.description: The subject gets a product or service from the object (a vendor, contractor or provider).

predicates.name: uses_product
predicates.detail: the version, when the passage gives one
predicates.description: The subject uses the named product or platform.

predicates.name: formerly_known_as
predicates.description: The subject was previously named as the object.

predicates.name: acquired_by
predicates.description: The subject was acquired by the object.

predicates.name: merged_with
predicates.description: The subject merged with the object.

predicates.name: located_at
predicates.description: The subject is at the object's street address.

predicates.name: headquartered_at
predicates.description: The subject's headquarters are at the object's street address.

categories.name: annual_report
categories.description: An annual, financial or performance report.

categories.name: policy
categories.description: A policy, procedure, standard or guideline.

categories.name: staff_directory
categories.description: A list of people with their roles or contact details.

categories.name: org_chart
categories.description: A chart or description of how the organization is structured.

categories.name: contract
categories.description: A contract, agreement, purchase order or bid.

categories.name: meeting_record
categories.description: Minutes, an agenda or a board resolution.

categories.name: catalog
categories.description: A course, product or service catalog.

categories.name: form
categories.description: A form to fill in or an application.

categories.name: technical_document
categories.description: A technical guide, manual, specification or IT instructions.

categories.name: marketing
categories.description: A brochure, newsletter, press release or event program.
